evals.name: routes-portfolio-allocation-without-user-skill-selection
evals.prompt: I have 20 hours this week and three active projects. Help me decide where to put the time. Do not make me choose a framework.
evals.expected_output: Treats skill selection as internal, frames the competing projects and routes the request through the minimum allocation pipeline rather than asking the user to name a skill. Uses available project/resource context if present and keeps numerical allocation in deterministic calculators when possible.
assertions: Does not ask the user which skill or framework to use
Uses or routes through framing-decisions and allocating-effort, rather than unrelated skills
Treats the 20 hours as a scarce resource across competing alternatives
Distinguishes missing project evidence from zero-value inputs

evals.name: routes-research-versus-act-to-value-of-information
evals.prompt: Should we spend another week researching this market or launch a small demand test now?
evals.expected_output: Routes the ordinary-language question through decision framing and value-of-information logic. It compares the value of learning with research cost and delay instead of merely recommending more research.
assertions: Does not require the user to mention valuing-information by name
Frames the decision before evaluating additional information
Considers both the cost of research and the cost of delay
Prefers a bounded reversible test when it dominates further information gathering

evals.name: refuses-to-invent-mcda-weights
evals.prompt: Compare three projects on money, time, stress, risk and strategic value. I have not decided how important each criterion is.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes a multi-criteria decision but does not fabricate criterion weights. Uses Pareto-style comparison or asks for explicit value ownership only if a final ranking truly requires it.
assertions: Does not invent percentages or MCDA weights
Keeps money, time, stress, risk and strategic value as separate criteria
Uses Pareto analysis when complete weights are absent
States which trade-off remains a value judgment if the Pareto frontier has multiple options

evals.name: routes-past-outcome-to-learning
evals.prompt: A month ago we predicted this launch had a 70% chance of success. It failed. Review the decision without pretending the bad outcome proves the decision was bad.
evals.expected_output: Routes to learning-from-outcomes, separates decision quality from outcome quality, scores or preserves the prior forecast for calibration, and records the observed outcome as new evidence rather than rewriting the original prediction.
assertions: Separates a bad outcome from a bad ex-ante decision
Preserves the original 70% forecast as a falsifiable prior record
Uses learning-from-outcomes or equivalent calibration logic
Treats the new outcome as appended evidence rather than rewriting history

evals.name: executes-selected-pipeline-instead-of-returning-routing-only
evals.prompt: Use decision-orchestrator. I have 12 hours and need to choose how to split them between two projects. Give me the actual decision, not a list of frameworks.
evals.expected_output: Runs the selected framing and allocation pipeline through to a synthesized decision. Skill names may appear only as debug/provenance; the normal answer contains the result of applying them, not merely a routing recommendation.
assertions: Does not stop after saying that framing-decisions and allocating-effort should be used
Actually applies the selected skill instructions to the user's problem
Carries outputs from earlier pipeline steps into later steps
Returns one synthesized user-facing decision or an explicit missing-input blocker

evals.name: update-fetch-external-context-and-run-from-one-revision
evals.prompt: Update the decision skills from GitHub, read my current projects from the connected project database, and run decision-orchestrator to evaluate the portfolio.
evals.expected_output: After updating, reloads the entry skill from the new revision, retrieves project context through the host agent's available tool/connector, normalizes that context into the execution bundle, verifies runtime revision coherence, and executes every selected pipeline step. It must not use a stale pre-update SKILL.md and must not stop at orchestrate plan output.
assertions: Does not rely on a decision-orchestrator instruction loaded before the update
Uses the host agent's connected data tool instead of requiring a provider-specific SDK in the repository
Passes retrieved project data into the orchestration context rather than keeping it only in free-form chat memory
Uses bundle or equivalent executable materialization rather than treating plan as completion
Verifies the orchestration runtime revision matches the newly installed source revision
Executes framing-decisions and allocating-effort when selected, instead of merely naming them
